stories.headline: 27 relief camps readied for residents of flood-prone areas in Sholinganallur and Perungudi
stories.title: 27 relief camps readied for residents of flood-prone areas in Sholinganallur and Perungudi
stories.summary: Minister K.Vignesh inspects monsoon preparedness in some of the most flood prone areas in the southern part of the city
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Excise and Prohibition Minister K. Vignesh on Monday reviewed the monsoon preparedness work in some of the most flood-prone areas in the southern parts of the city and ordered officials to expedite work on relief centres at 27 locations to help residents during the Northeast monsoon.
He also directed officials to complete work in three days.

Owing to the risk of heavy flooding in the southern parts of the city, the Minister directed the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) to expedite work on water supply, toilet facilities, power, and food for residents at relief centres.

The Minister ordered officials to prepare food for residents of flood-prone areas by facilitating the supply of food from 21 Amma Canteens in Perungudi, 17 Amma canteens in Sholinganallur, and six community kitchens.
The Minister advised.
THE GCC to appoint nodal officers to prepare the food for distribution.
He also directed officials to coordinate with fire and rescue services to catch snakes in flood-prone residential areas in the two zones during the monsoon.
In Sholinganallur zone, work on 95.7 km of drains has been completed.
Work on 13.385 km of drains is under way.
In Perungudi, 145.27 km of drains out of 154.19 km has been completed.
Work on 73 metres of drains in nine stretches is under way.
The Minister directed officials to expedite the work.

stories.headline: Punjab: Akali Dal to announce election manifesto on Nov 1
stories.title: Punjab: Akali Dal to announce election manifesto on Nov 1
stories.summary: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Saturday announced to organize a statewide yatra covering all assembly constituencies which will start from Sri Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo on November 10 and to announce election manifesto on November 1.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Saturday announced to organize a statewide yatra covering all assembly constituencies which will start from Sri Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo on November 10 and to announce election manifesto on November 1.

Chandigarh: The Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Saturday announced to organize a statewide yatra covering all assembly constituencies which will start from Sri Damdama Sahib in Talwandi Sabo on November 10 and to announce election manifesto on November 1.
The yatra, which will be led by party President Sukhbir Badal, will be conducted in three phases, with the first phase being held from November 10 to 22.
The second phase will be launched from Sri Anandpur Sahib and the third one from Sri Akal Takht Sahib.

Disclosing this after the culmination of a series of meetings with the party’s Scheduled Caste, Backward Class and Youth wing, which were presided over by Badal, senior leader Daljit Cheema said the party President took first-hand feedback on issues to be included in the party’s election manifesto as well as focusing on improving the party organisation.
He said the feedback received from the different party wings would be taken up for consideration in the next meeting of the party’s election manifesto committee on October 24.
“The manifesto will be released on November 1,” he added.

Badal told the media that the arrest of Amardeep Grewal, the brother-in-law of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s wife Gurpreet Kaur, would bring the corruption being done in the Chief Minister’s residence before the people.
“Be it Bhagwant Mann or his Arvind Kejriwal, the central agencies are closing in on all of them.
All of them will be booked and will face the consequences of their corrupt acts.”
Badal said the Chief Minister was directly responsible for the murder of anti-drug crusader Parvinder Singh Jhota.
He said instead of ending the drug menace, the Yudh Nasheyan Virudh campaign of the AAP government was resulting in the killing of anti-drug activists and whistleblowers.

stories.headline: New Deputy Election Commissioner appointed in ECI amid concerns over work hierarchy
stories.title: New Deputy Election Commissioner appointed in ECI amid concerns over work hierarchy
stories.summary: Prakash Rajpurohit fills the vacancy left by Sanjay Kumar’s premature repatriation, amid concerns raised by Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over IT department files not being routed through him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Prakash Rajpurohit, an IAS officer of the 2010 batch, has been appointed as a Deputy Election Commissioner in the Election Commission of India (ECI), filling the vacancy caused by the premature repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, who was incharge of the Electoral Rolls and IT division.

What will be the work allocation in the ECI after this new appointment is crucial, as Sanjay Kumar, who had been DEC from August 2024 till August this year, had been responsible for the electoral roll and IT divisions of the ECI, and had signed the ECI’s June 24, 2025, order initiating the SIR in the country.
It is also important because the two Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had written to the Cabinet Secretary on how files of the ECI.
IT department head Dr. Seema Khanna not being routed through Mr. Kumar, who was a seasoned officer, was a violation.
Dr. Khanna joined the ECI in 2025 on deputation from the National Informatics Centre.
She heads the commission’s.
IT department, and oversees its digital infrastructure, including systems for electoral-roll management.

According to Election Commission sources, before the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar to his parent cadre, Dr. Khanna’s files had been routed through him till she was given a promotion to Level 15, which is equivalent to the rank of an Additional Secretary.

Since Mr. Kumar was of the rank of a Joint Secretary (which is Level 14), Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Manish Garg issued an internal order that Dr. Khanna’s files should go straight to the Election Commissioners from then.
This order was, however, never implemented.

Dr. Khanna’s files started being routed through to Maneesh Garg himself following the repatriation of Sanjay Kumar, as he was his link officer, which made him responsible for his departments in his absence.
Mr. Rajpurohit’s appointment was cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet late on Saturday as per the order by the Department of Personnel and Training.

stories.headline: SC refuses to entertain plea for CBI probe into sale of tickets by UP-based political parties
stories.title: SC refuses to entertain plea for CBI probe into sale of tickets by UP-based political parties
stories.summary: The Supreme Court asked the petitioner to approach the Election Commission instead, after the Allahabad High Court had earlier declined to entertain the same plea
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) refused to entertain a plea seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into a sting operation on the alleged sale of tickets by some unrecognised political parties in Uttar Pradesh.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana granted liberty to the petitioner, Swaraj Vahini Association, to revive its representation and reminder pending with the Election Commission on the issue.
The Bench noted in the order that the Allahabad High Court had refused to entertain the Public Interest Litigation (PIL) of the petitioner association on the issue.
The plea referred to certain sting operations undertaken and shared on social media pertaining to the working of some political parties and the alleged sale of election tickets.
The Bench refused to entertain the plea and instead asked the petitioner to approach the poll panel.
“We have no reason to doubt that the poll panel will make endeavours to redress the grievances,” the order said.

Besides the Election Commission and the Centre, the plea has made the Chief Election Commissioner and the Uttar Pradesh-based Nishad Party, Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, Apna Dal Sone Lal and Jan Janvadi Party Socialist parties to the case.

On September 7, 2026, the Allahabad High Court dismissed the PIL seeking an investigation by the CBI or another investigating agency into a sting operation circulated on social media concerning the functioning of political parties.

A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Arun Bhansali and Justice Kshitij Shailendra declined to entertain the petition, observing that the court could not be expected to direct investigations into every sting operation or social media report presented in the name of public interest.

stories.headline: Chief justice inspects NIT Sikkim site for permanent law university campus
stories.title: Chief justice inspects NIT Sikkim site for permanent law university campus
stories.summary: Chief justice inspects NIT Sikkim site for permanent law university campus
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: Chief Justice A Muhamed Mustaque inspected NIT Sikkim's Ravangla campus and adjoining land.
The assessment will determine whether the site can support the law university's permanent facilities.

A Muhamed Mustaque on Saturday inspected the National Institute of Technology campus at Ravangla to assess whether it could house the permanent campus of Sikkim National Law University, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
The inspection covered the campus infrastructure, accommodation facilities and adjoining land that could be used for the proposed university's academic, administrative and residential needs.
According to an official statement cited by PTI, Justice Mustaque sought details about the use of classrooms, faculty quarters, the conference hall and the library.
He also enquired about land available for future expansion and outlined the infrastructure needed to meet the academic and residential requirements of students and faculty members.
Revenue Officer Rinzing Wangyal Bhutia briefed the delegation on the layout of the campus, which covers about 9.23 acres, and its existing infrastructure.
He also identified adjoining land parcels that could potentially accommodate additional facilities for the law university.

NIT Sikkim Dean of Students' Welfare Ranjan Basak informed the delegation about the institute's functioning, student enrolment across departments, accommodation facilities, water supply and waste management systems, PTI reported.
Basak also provided details about the construction of NIT Sikkim's permanent campus at Khamdong near Singtam and the institute's phased relocation to the new premises.
Justice Mustaque toured various infrastructure blocks and inspected multipurpose halls, water tanks, the playground and accommodation facilities for students and faculty members.

The delegation included High Court Registrar General Karma Wangchuk Bhutia, Law and Parliamentary Affairs Department Secretary Suraj Chettri, Buildings and Housing Department Principal Chief Engineer Yadunandan Gautam, and SNLU Vice-Chancellor-in-Charge Rajendra Dhar Dubey.

stories.headline: CJI Surya Kant to visit Ladakh tomorrow to inaugurate Ladakh Bench of High Court
stories.title: CJI Surya Kant to visit Ladakh tomorrow to inaugurate Ladakh Bench of High Court
stories.summary: Ladakh, Oct 17: The Chief Justice of India, Justice Surya Kant, will visit Ladakh on Sunday to inaugurate the newly constituted Ladakh bench of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra said at a press conference today. He said the CJI will be accompanied by four Supreme Court judges, the chief justice of the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court, and other high court judges. The attorney general of India will also attend the event, he said. “It is a very big thing. Frankly speaking in recent times, if you scan the history of the High Courts in India, I don't think that in the last 40 years any sitting bench has been set up in this fashion for any other High Court. The only example which comes to my mind is maybe that of the North Eastern States, where the Guwahati High Court, had benches in Arunachal Pradesh, where I have worked,” he said. “Justice coming closer to the people is a very big thing,” the CS said. “Otherwise, anyone who was aggrieved and wanted to file a writ petition would have to go to Srinagar or Jammu. I think the fact that this is now possible here in Ladakh is an extremely positive development,” he added. He said the bench was established within two months and was not among the demands raised during negotiations, describing it as a unilateral initiative by the Centre. Negotiations are currently underway between Ladakhi political leaders and the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Ladakhi leaders are seeking a Union Territory with a legislature and constitutional safeguards under Article 371. “The Government of India fully understands how difficult this terrain is, the challenging circumstances in which people live here and how crucial it is to ensure that justice is accessible closer to their doorstep,” Kundra said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court-appointed panel launches portal for complaints over July violence at Jantar Mantar
stories.title: Supreme Court-appointed panel launches portal for complaints over July violence at Jantar Mantar
stories.summary: The MHA said that priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence, harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court-appointed High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) has launched a portal to enquire into all aspects of the incidents relating to violence at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, and at places outside Delhi, during the month of July 2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said on Saturday (October 17, 2026).

The MHA said that priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence, harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side.
“The portal, http://hpec.nic.in, has been launched for the convenience of the affected people, including police personnel,” it said.
The Committee will examine issues outlined in the Supreme Court’s order.
“The portal has been designed to protect vulnerable witnesses and allow affected people to keep their identities confidential, if they wish to do so,” it said.
“Affected people and other stakeholders have been encouraged to submit complaints and representations through the portal using the applicable formats,” the MHA said.
Anyone wishing to provide information or suggestions on issues referred to the Committee under the two court orders can also use the portal.

“Complaints, representations and other relevant material can also be submitted in person at the Committee’s office at Shiksha Sadan, 17 Rouse Avenue Institutional Area, New Delhi, between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. on working days,” it said.
“Submissions can also be sent by post to the same address or by email to hpec2026.enquiry@nic.in,” it said.

Supreme Court had constituted a five-member HPEC to enquire into all aspects of the incidents of violence at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and at places outside the national capital during July 2026, including the broader issues surrounding the incidents.

Besides Justice Reddy, the Committee comprises former Punjab and Haryana High Court Chief Justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi High Court judge Justice Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP L.R. Bishnoi.

The Supreme Court ordered the constitution of the Committee while hearing a batch of pleas alleging police excesses against student protesters during the agitation spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), alongside allegations of violence against police personnel.

stories.headline: Delhi court issues bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee
stories.title: Delhi court issues bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 17 : A Delhi court has issued a bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in an eight-year-old criminal defamation case filed by Vikas Pandey, after being informed that a fresh summons issued could not be served as the premises of his residence was found locked. The Saket Courts passed the order on Saturday after being apprised that the service of summons on Rathee remained incomplete. The court has now listed the matter for further hearing on October 31. In an order passed earlier this month, the court had permitted fresh summons to be served on Rathee through dasti service, allowing the complainant to accompany the process server to facilitate service. Despite the steps taken, the court was informed that the notice could not be served as the premises of Rathee's house was locked, leading to the issuance of the bailable warrant. The case pertains to a video titled 'BJP IT Cell Part 2', which allegedly defamed Pandey. The video was also retweeted by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal in 2018, who later acknowledged before the Supreme Court that he had made a mistake by retweeting it. Pandey, the founder of the social media page 'I Support Narendra Modi', had claimed that the retweet had tarnished his reputation. The proceedings against Rathee had remained pending amid repeated difficulties in serving summons on him since 2019, with the complainant claiming that his continued absence from India had delayed the case. Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria. The matter had also reached the Supreme Court in connection with Kejriwal's challenge to the criminal defamation proceedings arising from the retweet. In February 2024, Kejriwal told the apex court that he had made a mistake by sharing the video. A Bench of Justices Sanjiv Khanna, who later became Chief Justice of India (CJI) and has since retired, and Dipankar Datta had stayed the trial court proceedings against Kejriwal while hearing his plea challenging the Delhi High Court's refusal to quash the summons issued against him. The Delhi High Court had earlier upheld the summoning order, observing that retweeting allegedly defamatory content could attract prosecution under Section 499 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). --IANS

stories.headline: India's Russian crude binge to continue after Trump waives new sanctions law
stories.title: India's Russian crude binge to continue after Trump waives new sanctions law
stories.summary: India is the largest importer of Russian seaborne crude, averaging 1.8 million barrels per day this year, ahead of China at 1.2 million
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India is expected to keep importing Russian crude at close to current levels after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs mandated by a new law on major buyers of Russian oil, analysts said.

Trump issued an executive order late on Friday waiving the "sanctions, restrictions, and duties" under the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, a day before a 30-day deadline for enforcement expired.
He signed the law on September 18.
The law authorised tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from the five largest importers of Russian crude and gas, and sanctions on Russia's shadow fleet of tankers.
The waiver is not specific to India and could also benefit China.
The order lets the administration reconsider it later.
India is the largest importer of Russian seaborne crude, averaging 1.8 million barrels per day this year, ahead of China at 1.2 million, ship tracking data showed.
Italy, Turkey and the Netherlands completed the top five.
India took about 1.82 million bpd of Russian crude in September against about 1.49 million for China.
Kpler expects October imports to hold at around 1.8-1.9 million bpd.
Volumes are well below mid-year highs.
Indian imports peaked at 2.6 million bpd in June and 2.57 million bpd in July.
